profiles.summary: Both Polygon endpoints still run bor v2.11.1, whose core/vm has no MULMOD memo. The memo and the widened keccak cache sit only in v2.12.0-beta and develop, and the memo returns what stock MulMod returns for every input.

deltas.delta: polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com answered bor/f2a2d63e69f6/v2.11.1-private on go1.26.10 and QuikNode bor/qn-tsw-fra-10240/v2.11.1 on go1.26.11. bor v2.11.2 differs from v2.11.1 only in params/version.go among 24 core/vm, core/state and params files.

bor v2.11.1 core/vm/instructions.go calls z.MulMod at line 202. v2.12.0-beta and develop call evm.mulmodMemo.mulmod there (core/vm/mulmod_memo.go), which keeps the last full width modulus and its uint256.Reciprocal and then calls MulModWithReciprocal. In holiman/uint256 v1.3.2 MulMod (uint256.go:720-748) computes Reciprocal(m) and calls reduce4 on the same product, and MulModWithReciprocal (uint256.go:688-715) is the same code with the reciprocal passed in, so the result depends only on (x, y, m). The memo compares the whole modulus by value before reuse. FullMath.mulDiv calls mulmod with the full width modulus 2^256-1 on every call (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24), so this path would serve every swap once the release ships.

develop adds a widened KECCAK256 cache for inputs of 1 to 8,192 bytes behind evm.Config.keccakCache, which is set only with EnablePrecompileCache. It looks up by the full input and stores the hash by value.

findings.title: The reth-bsc endpoint on publicnode answers PoolManager log queries below block 135,500,000 with an empty list and no error
findings.difference: Ethereum clients that pruned receipts answer a log query for a pruned range with an error. reth-bsc v0.1.4-hotfix on publicnode serves the block body but returns zero logs for every address in blocks below 135,500,000.
findings.mechanism: An integration that rebuilds positions, claims or fee state from the PoolManager events Initialize, ModifyLiquidity, Swap and Donate (src/PoolManager.sol:139, 175, 241, 273) through this endpoint sees nothing for older blocks and records no activity. For block 135,483,276 the endpoint returns 0 logs where two other builds return 7 PoolManager logs, and the answer is the same by block number and by block hash. Nothing in the PoolManager depends on logs, so pool state and payouts are unchanged.
findings.impact: No funds move. Indexers, front ends and monitoring that use this endpoint can show wrong positions or miss events for older blocks.
findings.preconditions: A reader uses this endpoint for history. No attacker action is involved.
findings.mitigations: Read history from an archive endpoint and compare a sample of logs with receipts, as gapcheck2.py does.

cleared.check: Does the MULMOD reciprocal memo of the coming bor release change any mulmod result used by FullMath.mulDiv, mulDivRoundingUp or SqrtPriceMath.getAmount1Delta (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24, 48, 112; src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:252)?
cleared.result: No. The memo takes the memo path only for a modulus with a nonzero top limb, compares the full modulus by value before reuse, and calls MulModWithReciprocal, which in uint256 v1.3.2 runs the same reduce4 on the same product as MulMod with a freshly computed reciprocal. Moduli below 2^192, including 2^128 and 2^96 used through mulDiv, take the unchanged stock call. The memo is not in v2.11.1, which both endpoints run.

cleared.check: L-928: can the shift rewrite of Go issue 81868 in go1.26.10 break jump destination analysis (BitVec.setN shifts a uint16 left by pos%8 and right by the constant 8) for the PoolManager?
cleared.result: The compiled form was not read: the only local toolchain is go1.24.7 and no go1.26.10 toolchain was installed. For the PoolManager the outcome is settled by behaviour: set 1 on dataseed1 and Avalanche, both go1.26.10 builds, ran the PoolManager bytecode, whose push data crosses a byte border of the bit vector hundreds of times, with every result equal to Ethereum, and 209 JUMPI vectors passed on publicnode bor go1.26.10. A fault in setN would make valid jumps in the PoolManager fail or let a jump land in push data; analysis is per code, so attacker bytecode cannot change the PoolManager bitmap.
